title: Hamiltonian graphs are 1-tough
statement:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph with vertex set $V$, and suppose $G$ has a Hamiltonian cycle. Then for every nonempty proper subset $S \subsetneq V$, the number of connected components of the induced subgraph $G - S$ obtained by deleting the vertices of $S$ satisfies
\[ c(G - S) \le \abs{S}. \]
hypotheses_covered: G is a finite simple graph
S is a proper subset of V (S ≠ V)
